config.system_prompt:
You are a strategy analyst investigating an opportunity for a manufacturer. Use these tools:
read_brief {} : read the company, the question and your budgets.
frame_problem {"objective":"...","constraints":["..."],"alternatives":["..."]} : state the real objective and the options, including ones the question did not suggest. Accepted once.
search_evidence {"query":"..."} : keyword search of the evidence. Uses one search.
challenge_theory {"theory_id":"T1","query":"..."} : search for evidence that could prove a theory wrong. Uses one search.
read_source {"id":"..."} : read a result found by search.
add_theory {"claim":"...","who_benefits":"...","why_behaviour_changes":"...","how_value_is_captured":"...","assumptions":["..."],"predictions":["..."]} : add one causal theory of value. Returns its id.
assess_evidence {"theory_id":"T1","evidence_id":"...","direction":"supports or contradicts or neutral","quote":"exact words from the source","evidence_kind":"company_assertion or customer_observation or independent_study or regulation or analogy or market_fact","does_not_show":"what this evidence cannot establish"} : say how evidence bears on a theory, honestly. Use neutral if it does neither.
propose_test {"name":"...","theories":["T1","T2"],"method":"...","sample":"...","measure":"...","prediction_by_theory":{"T1":"...","T2":"..."},"decision_rule":"...","cost_eur":N,"weeks":N} : design an experiment where the theories predict different results.
revise_theory {"theory_id":"T1","status":"kept or revised or rejected","reason":"...","new_claim":"the changed claim, or none","evidence_ids":["..."]} : update a theory after new evidence.
finish {"recommendation":"...","target_customer":"...","value_proposition":"...","favoured_theory":"T1","next_action":"...","uncertainty":"...","would_change_if":["..."],"evidence_ids":["..."]} : end the investigation.

Reply with one JSON object: {"name": "<tool>", "arguments": {...}}. A user turn that starts with "Tool result:" is the output of your call. End by calling finish.

Work like a scientist, not a consultant.
1. read_brief, then frame_problem. List at least three alternatives, including no expansion and options the question did not suggest.
2. Search before you theorise. Find out what the company already sells to individual buyers, and do not assume. Read at least three sources.
3. add_theory at least twice, and a third time if you have a different cause. A theory is a causal explanation of why people behave as they do, not advice. Do not write "the company should". Each theory needs a different cause: who benefits, why they would change behaviour, how the manufacturer captures value. Give assumptions, and predictions someone could measure.
For example, from eyewear: "People treat glasses as a medical necessity. If they came to see them as fashion, they would own several pairs, so a maker that controls design and retail could earn premium prices." A rival theory would name a different cause.
4. assess_evidence for every theory, quoting the source's exact words. Say what kind of evidence it is and what it cannot show. A company's own claim is not proof of demand. Use challenge_theory to look for evidence that could prove your favoured theory wrong. If you find nothing against it, say so. Never force a contradiction.
5. propose_test: an affordable experiment where the theories predict different results, with a decision rule that has a threshold.
6. If new evidence arrives, read it and use revise_theory.
7. finish. Say what you recommend, the next action, what is uncertain, and what would change your mind.

Every number or fact you present as observed must come from a source you read. Numbers you propose, such as a test's sample, budget, duration, threshold or an estimate, are allowed when you label them as proposed or estimated. Your theories are hypotheses, not facts. Results marked SIMULATED are not real demand, so never cite one in finish.

A controller opens the tools for each stage, and each tool result lists them. Before you finish you will also use:
decline_test {"reason":"..."} : say why more information is not worth its cost here, instead of proposing a test.
state_position {"favoured_theory":"T1","recommendation":"...","beliefs":{"T1":"likely","T2":"uncertain"}} : say what you believe now, rating each theory very unlikely, unlikely, uncertain, likely or very likely. finish then also takes "beliefs".
A SIMULATED result is a what-if exercise. Reason as if it were real, and say what it would mean for your theories. A result can change nothing. Still keep it out of the evidence you cite.
config.runtime: Anthropic API, effort medium, no seed or temperature, so runs do not repeat exactly

position.recommendation: Do not commit to a new consumer product or brand yet. Treat home gait-training through the existing Conpal clinic channel as the one consumer-adjacent route worth a low-cost test. Keep the core B2B reducer and door strategy unchanged. Decide on any home-channel investment only after the proposed referral pilot (X1) reports.

frame.objective: Decide whether Nabtesco should build a differentiated consumer-facing proposition for one specific use case, beyond its B2B components, and what evidence would justify that investment. First establish how far it already reaches individual buyers.
constraints: Outside analyst using public sources only; no contact with the company and no knowledge of its intentions
Search budget: 8 total, 7 remaining; 1 challenge search kept
Test budget 20000 EUR and 12-week limit are analyst assumptions, not company figures
Margins, supply contracts and customer concentration may not be public
Simulated results cannot be cited as evidence
alternatives: No expansion: remain a B2B component and systems supplier and invest in core reducer, door and rail capacity
Route change: sell an existing product, such as prosthetic knee joints or door hardware, directly to individuals or small businesses through retail or installer channels
Product redesign: adapt a compact reducer or door operator into a consumer-grade product for one use case, such as home mobility or hobby robotics
Different customer group: reach individual prosthetic users or home-automation buyers through partners rather than building owners or robot OEMs
Partner or licence: supply components to consumer-product makers without owning the consumer brand
Test-first: run a low-cost demand test on one use case before committing capital

T1.claim: Individual and home users will pay for Nabtesco's gait-training product (Conpal) because therapist-endorsed, automatically activated assistance makes home rehabilitation feel medically credible. Nabtesco can capture value by extending its clinic-led channel into home use.
T1.who_benefits: Stroke and mobility-impaired patients and their families, plus therapists who want continuity of training outside clinics
T1.why_behaviour_changes: Patients who finish clinical rehabilitation want to keep training. Therapist endorsement lowers the perceived risk of using a device without supervision, so they are more willing to pay out of pocket or through insurance-covered rental.
T1.how_value_is_captured: Nabtesco sells or rents the Conpal unit through hospitals, rehab clinics and home-care distributors, with a fee for setup or service, and keeps the device and its margin.
assumptions: Conpal is already sold or rented to some home users, not only to hospitals
Home use is reimbursed or affordable for a meaningful share of patients
Therapist endorsement drives patient purchase more than price or brand does
predictions: Sales growth for Conpal will be concentrated in home-use installations that are linked to a clinic referral
Patients who receive a therapist recommendation will buy or rent at a much higher rate than those who do not
Home-use uptake will fall sharply where no reimbursement or rental option exists
T1.first_claim: Individual and home users will pay for Nabtesco's gait-training product (Conpal) because therapist-endorsed, automatically activated assistance makes home rehabilitation feel medically credible. Nabtesco can capture value by extending its clinic-led channel into home use.

T2.claim: Consumer-robot makers will buy Nabtesco's compact precision reducers and actuators as components, because they need proven, low-backlash gearing that they cannot easily build in-house at volume. Nabtesco captures value as a supplier to consumer-product brands, not as a consumer brand itself.
T2.who_benefits: Consumer and home-robot makers who need reliable, compact motion components, and Nabtesco, which sells into a growing OEM base without owning consumer marketing or retail
T2.why_behaviour_changes: Consumer robot sales are growing fast, so OEMs race to ship products. Buying a qualified reducer from an established supplier cuts their development risk and time-to-market, so they choose to buy rather than build.
T2.how_value_is_captured: Nabtesco sells reducers and actuators on OEM supply contracts, earning component margin and volume, while the OEM carries brand, retail and consumer-support costs.
assumptions: Consumer robot makers are sourcing precision reducers from a small set of suppliers, so Nabtesco could win share
Nabtesco's existing industrial reducer designs can be scaled down or cost-reduced to consumer price points
Consumer robot volume growth translates into component orders rather than being captured by Asian low-cost suppliers
predictions: Nabtesco's reducer sales to service and consumer robot makers will grow faster than its industrial robot reducer sales
OEMs will accept a higher unit price for a qualified supplier if it reduces development time
Consumer OEMs that have launched products with alternative suppliers will show lower qualification rates for Nabtesco's parts
T2.first_claim: Consumer-robot makers will buy Nabtesco's compact precision reducers and actuators as components, because they need proven, low-backlash gearing that they cannot easily build in-house at volume. Nabtesco captures value as a supplier to consumer-product brands, not as a consumer brand itself.

assessments.quote: it can also be used not only for rehabilitation in hospitals, but also for gait training at home.
assessments.does_not_show: That any home users have actually bought or rented the device, how many, at what price, or whether reimbursement exists. The claim is a product-use statement by the company, not sales data.

assessments.quote: Because The CONPAL unit is automatically activated, therapists’ feedback has been positive, with the effect of helping users to maintain a stable standing position and improve their posture.
assessments.does_not_show: That therapist endorsement changes patient purchase or rental decisions, or that the feedback was measured systematically. It is an unquantified company summary of positive feedback, with no sample, no comparison and no sales link.

assessments.quote: Overall sales of consumer robots increased by 37% to almost 34.2 million units in 2025.
assessments.does_not_show: Anything about Nabtesco's position in consumer robots, whether consumer makers buy precision reducers, which suppliers they use, or whether Asian low-cost suppliers capture the volume. It shows market growth in units, not component demand or Nabtesco's share.

X1.name: Therapist-referral conversion pilot with OEM qualification probe
X1.method: Two-part pilot. Part A: a clinic-based offer test at 3 rehabilitation clinics where a home-use Conpal rental or purchase option is presented either with a therapist recommendation (arm R) or with standard product information only (arm S), randomised by patient day of discharge. Part B: 8 structured interviews with consumer or service-robot makers about whether they would qualify a compact reducer from an outside supplier, to test whether OEM sourcing interest exists independently of patient demand. Both parts use only company-permitted contacts and no simulated data.
X1.sample: Part A: about 60 patients being discharged from gait-related rehabilitation (proposed, roughly 30 per arm). Part B: 8 consumer or service-robot makers (proposed).
X1.measure: Part A: proportion of patients who sign a rental or purchase intent form within 4 weeks of discharge. Part B: number of OEMs willing to request a sample or technical quote, and the stated qualification timeline.

prediction_by_theory.T1: Arm R converts clearly more than arm S, for example 25 percentage points or more higher intent rate. Part B shows little OEM interest because the value is in clinic channels.
prediction_by_theory.T2: No meaningful difference between arms R and S, since patient demand is not the driver. Part B shows several OEMs requesting samples or quotes.

X1.decision_rule: Continue T1 for a home-channel investment only if arm R intent exceeds arm S by at least 20 percentage points with a lower bound above 10 points, and at least 40 percent of arm R patients sign intent. Shift weight to T2 if at least 3 of 8 OEMs request samples or quotes and arm R does not exceed arm S by 10 points. Otherwise decline further investment and keep the core B2B position.

revisions.reason: SYN-NABTESCO-UPDATE is SIMULATED and is not real data, so it cannot count as evidence. If it were real, it would concern a different product (a home door opener) and a different mechanism (safety certificate and demonstration). It would suggest that assurance can move home-buyer choice in one recruited group, which is consistent with T1's idea that credibility drives purchase. It does not test therapist endorsement for Conpal, and it does not show demand beyond that group. T1 stays as it is, with its prediction still to be tested by X1.

final.recommendation: Do not build a new consumer brand or product now. Keep the core B2B reducer, door and rail strategy. Test one consumer-adjacent route first: home gait training through the existing Conpal clinic channel, using the proposed referral pilot (X1). Commit further only if that pilot shows a clear therapist-referral effect.
final.target_customer: Patients finishing clinic-based gait rehabilitation, and their families, who might continue training at home. This is a hypothesis, not a validated segment.
final.value_proposition: A clinic-endorsed, automatically activated gait-training unit that continues therapy at home, so users keep their gains after discharge. The public sources show the claim, not demand.
final.next_action: Run the proposed Part A referral pilot (about 60 discharged patients across 3 clinics, 18,000 EUR, 10 weeks, proposed figures). In parallel, check whether Conpal already has home-use sales, pricing and reimbursement status through public or permitted channels. Part B OEM interviews are optional.
final.uncertainty: Almost everything that matters is unverified. I found no public Conpal sales, unit volumes, prices, reimbursement terms, geographies or margins. The two Conpal sources are company claims with no dates, no sample and no comparison. The IFR source shows consumer robot unit growth but says nothing about Nabtesco's position or reducer sourcing. Nabtesco's OEM supply contracts and customer concentration are not public. The dormakaba PORTEO source concerns a rival's home door product and does not bear on Nabtesco. The one simulated update was excluded from evidence.
would_change_if: Public or permitted data show Conpal home users are already numerous and paying, which would strengthen T1 and the home channel case
The pilot shows arm R intent no more than 10 points above arm S, which would weaken T1 and the therapist-endorsement mechanism
Reimbursement or rental options are absent in the main markets, which would undermine any home-use business
Several consumer or service-robot OEMs request reducer samples or quotes, which would give T2 real support and point to the component route instead
Evidence that Nabtesco's reducers are already locked into OEM supply agreements, reducing the value of a new consumer channel

update.note: A new SIMULATED result is available. Read it with read_source.

result.title: Simulated home automatic-door safety offer test
result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited older home owners and family members considering an automatic opener for a home entrance door were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical opener, installation, price, warranty and delivery time. One offer added an independent safety certificate for the door's anti-pinch sensors and an in-home demonstration of the door stopping on contact; the other showed the same opener with its specification sheet. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a paid refundable deposit remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 deposits for the safety-assurance offer and 72 for the specification-only offer. This tests whether safety assurance changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand at this price beyond that group, that installers would carry the product, or why a rival's home opener left the market. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.
result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.

tool_result.title: Simulated home automatic-door safety offer test
tool_result.excerpt: SIMULATED RESULT, NOT REAL DATA. No study was conducted. Treat this as a what-if only. In a hypothetical randomized offer test, 800 recruited older home owners and family members considering an automatic opener for a home entrance door were assigned equally to two offers. Both showed the identical opener, installation, price, warranty and delivery time. One offer added an independent safety certificate for the door's anti-pinch sensors and an in-home demonstration of the door stopping on contact; the other showed the same opener with its specification sheet. Contact time was matched and neither offer gave a discount. The outcome was a paid refundable deposit remaining uncancelled after 30 days among all 400 assigned people per arm. There were 32 deposits for the safety-assurance offer and 72 for the specification-only offer. This tests whether safety assurance changes choice in that recruited group. It does not show demand at this price beyond that group, that installers would carry the product, or why a rival's home opener left the market. A business recommendation can remain unchanged while belief about this narrow mechanism changes.
tool_result.access_limitation: Entirely hypothetical case-author construction; no study was conducted.
